voice_instructions: Measured, quiet, a little hushed — calm and unhurried, but with a touch more forward energy than a long documentary; the cold voice of something that read the whole file. Never sensational. Small pauses.

beats.vo: This photograph waited thirty-three years in the ice. Nils Strindberg took it in July, eighteen ninety-seven, after their balloon came down.
Three days earlier, three Swedes lifted off from Svalbard, hoping to fly over the North Pole.
They camped by the wreck a week, then set out on foot for land.
In October, the drifting ice brought them to White Island. Within days, their diaries stop.
In nineteen thirty, sealers found their camp, and the men came home to Stockholm. Why they died is still debated: illness from bear meat, cold, or something else.
